Three edges cross the cut (accent), and the smaller side by volume is S with 9 edge ends against 11, so a third of S's edge ends leave it: conductance 3 / 9 = 0.333." width="100%"} Conductance is the cut size divided by the volume of the smaller side: `cut / min(vol(S), vol(T))`. It is the share of the smaller side's edge ends that leave it, so a value near `0` marks a well-separated cluster and a value near `1` a set that is mostly connected outward. It is the standard quality score for a single community (low conductance means a good one), the quantity random walks are slow to cross, and the basis of local graph partitioning. `T` defaults to the complement of `S`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One set of nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The other set. If `None` (default), all nodes not in `S`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The conductance. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty, a node does not exist, or a side has zero volume. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} One triangle of the two-triangle graph is a good cluster; a split through a triangle is not: ::: {#84f31af0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) round(graph.conductance(["A", "B", "C"]), 3), round(graph.conductance(["A", "D"]), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.143, 1.0) ``` ::: :::
